title: Collect a range of numbers
description:
Write a function `range_values(start, end)` that returns a list of every integer from `start` to `end`, inclusive, in ascending order if `start <= end`, descending order otherwise.

Covers source items 1-2 ('iterate 0 to 10 with a for loop, then do the same with a while loop' and '10 to 0') as one exercise - a for loop and a while loop that visit the same values produce the same observable result, so this exercise checks that result rather than which loop keyword was used.
hints: Function to consider: range(), with a step argument
range(start, end, step) can count either up or down depending on the sign of step - a positive step counts up, a negative one counts down, and the stop value needs an extra +1 or -1 to be included.
Compare start and end to decide the step (1 or -1), then build a list from a range() call using that step and an inclusive-adjusted stop value.
expected_behavior: Returns the inclusive range from start to end, ascending or descending as needed.
explanation: range()'s third argument controls direction as well as size of the step - a for loop over range(start, end, -1) counts down exactly as naturally as range(start, end, 1) counts up.
